rationale: Asset-light, success-fee commercial brokerage legal in IL without registration. But fee level, lender broker-acceptance and 1-2 closes/month are all unsourced; unknown entrant faces credibility wall vs bank RMs and established CRE advisors; 6-month ramp, lumpy, rate/CRE-cycle exposed; producers take relationships. Realistic yr3-5 ~$60-120k.
red_flags: 1-2 closes/month by yr3 assumed for unknown entrant
Walker & Dunlop incumbent economics used as spending evidence

rationale: Only hard comp datum is SmartBiz 2% (~$3k/deal); lead cost and funded rate MISSING. Extreme competition from national marketplaces and thousands of ISOs; buyers start online. CPA-referral wedge plausible but slow. Low ticket implies volume grind; drift toward MCA is a known failure mode. Realistic ~$40-70k.
red_flags: Lead cost per funded deal MISSING
Survey application rates used as demand proxy, not obtainable demand
Lendio franchise gone and National Funding at capacity signal channel saturation

rationale: Strongest brokerage niche: large tickets ($1-5M), self-identifying national buyers, business-broker referral loop, fee rules documented [A]. AI spreading/credit-memo work is a real edge. But 12-25 closes/yr is unsupported, lender referral fees unpublished, free lender BDOs compete, SBA policy swings (2025 SOP tightening). Base ~$100-150k plausible by yr4-5.
red_flags: Non-contingent applicant fees hard to sell vs free BDOs
IL SOS registration status is analyst reading

rationale: Core assumption is weak: banks and CDCs package 504/7(a) for free, so owners rarely pay. Projects are infrequent (1-3 per decade per owner) and 90-150 day cycles; CPA channel unproven. Better as an add-on to WS01-003 than standalone. Fee caps are documented but paid-agent volume is MISSING.
red_flags: Share of SBA loans using paid agents MISSING
Directly competes with free bank/CDC packaging

rationale: Recurring per-loan B2B flow, national and delegable, AI-assisted processing genuinely useful. But founder lacks SBA expertise and must fund a scarce veteran hire before contracts; bank vendor diligence plus SBA LSP review means 3-12 month cycles; per-loan pricing entirely guessed. $500k ceiling claim is unsupported.
red_flags: Requires SBA veteran on equity/profit share — unverified

rationale: Record itself concedes economics rest on renewals/stacking and outbound calling/texting — the framework's named G3 example. Commission and clawback terms MISSING; state broker registration/disclosure regimes expanding; TCPA class-action tail. Easy customer access does not offset structural harm and enforcement risk.

Dealer vendor programs can create repeat monthly flow with short deal cycles; true leases are lightly regulated; dealers are publicly listable. But 3-6 point broker comp, funder onboarding of a new broker, and clawback terms are all unverified; captives and bank vendor programs entrenched; capex-cyclical. Realistic ~$70-120k.
red_flags: ELFA $1.5T is market size, not obtainable demand

rationale: Near-zero capital and a possible trailing-commission book, but commission structure (upfront vs life-of-client) is unpublished; need is episodic; factors sell direct. Record itself says solo for years and low delegation. Recurring residuals could be the redeeming feature if verified.
red_flags: Trailing commission existence/size unverified — the whole thesis
Triumph yield is incumbent factor economics, not broker economics

rationale: New carriers are public (FMCSA) but every factor and lender already hammers them; factoring referral fees MISSING; per-carrier value low; new-carrier failure and fraud rates high; freight-cycle exposed. Hard to see a durable $100k+ business as a pure referral desk.
red_flags: Competes with factors' own direct marketing
High new-carrier failure and identity fraud

rationale: Real, documented channel (UWM data, small-broker receipts) but founder must pass MLO licensing/credit fitness (credit unknown) and first work under another licensee; company license needs $50k net worth plus bonds. Extremely crowded, realtor relationships loyal, volume swings with rates; comp tightly regulated. Commodity product, weak wedge.
red_flags: Must be employed by a licensee first — slow path to own shop

rationale: Among the best-evidenced brokerages: Kiavi publishes up to 2.5% YSP [B]; investors are identifiable from deed records, borrow repeatedly, cycles 2-6 weeks. Business-purpose appears outside IL RMLA but IDFPR position unconfirmed; realized YSP likely below max; heavy competition and purpose-fraud liability. Base ~$80-150k.
red_flags: IDFPR stance on business-purpose 1-4 unit brokering MISSING

rationale: Plausible niche where banks retreated, permit data gives targets, and builders borrow per project. But fewer, slower closes than DSCR, comp unpublished, builder-failure risk, housing-cycle exposed. Better as a line inside WS01-011 than standalone.

Under-penetrated product with large ticket sizes, but every economic number is MISSING: active IL programs, deal counts, fee norms. 6-12 month cycles with mortgage-lender consent; national C-PACE lenders originate directly; technical sale few owners understand. High variance, slow first revenue (~9 months).

Record admits no strong entry strategy, unknown whether ag lenders pay brokers, and farmers bank locally and loyally with Farm Credit. Outsider credibility very low, transactions few, seasonal. No evidence an intermediary role exists.
red_flags: Whether ag lenders pay broker fees MISSING
No identified buyer demand for intermediaries

rationale: Spending evidence and compensation are entirely MISSING; platforms run their own sales teams and can cut residuals unilaterally; possible consumer loan-broker status under IL LBA. Field-sales rep business with commoditized product and no wedge.

Record concedes no defensible entry; economics depend on embedded dealer fees with consumer-protection exposure and contractor misrepresentation risk; consumer LBA/RMLA licensing if dwelling-secured. No data on any economics.
red_flags: Arranger liability for contractor sales misrepresentation

rationale: Media-arbitrage business against entrenched comparison sites and AI search answers; payouts MISSING; media spend upfront with net-30+ payouts; TCPA/consent and LBA exposure. AI content is commodity. Volatile, platform-dependent, no wedge.

Real need (large first-time practice loans) and good modeling wedge, but specialist practice lenders sell direct and practice brokers/CPAs already gatekeep financing. Referral-fee norms and deal counts MISSING. Niche overlap with WS01-003; few deals per year limit ceiling.

IRS flags ROBS as questionable; client retirement-savings losses create legal/reputational risk; franchise brokers already own the channel with funding partners; referral fees MISSING. Small, sporadic fees with no wedge.

Incumbent data is solid [B] but shows ~12% ROE with leverage; on $100k own capital this is ~$10-14k/yr before losses, concentrated in 1-2 loans with adverse selection. Puts the entire conditional backing at risk; scaling needs securities-regulated outside capital. A capital-allocation tool, not a first operating business.
red_flags: Adverse selection: national lenders take best borrowers

rationale: Consumer-purpose residential note purchasing appears to need an RMLA license with $150k net worth — above the founder's capital — plus licensed servicing. Capital locked for years in judicial foreclosure; pricing data MISSING; sellers prefer established buyers. Not viable at this scale.
red_flags: RMLA purchasing license net worth exceeds capital

rationale: Direct-mail finder business with low response rates, sporadic one-off deals, unclear legality (RMLA brokering, possible securities). No spending evidence or fee norms. Low ceiling and founder-bound.
red_flags: Legal status of brokering residential notes unresolved

rationale: Real recurring product with B-level incumbent yields, no IL license, and AI-useful verification. But own-capital returns ~10-20% after losses on $100k (~$10-20k/yr); one fraud loss can wipe years; bank lines for sub-$1M factors unverified. Scalable only after track record and leverage.
red_flags: Fraud is the dominant loss risk per incumbent

rationale: Holding the credits other funders decline is adverse selection by design; capital locked 24-60 months; discount-bank access needs track record; economics entirely MISSING. Low-teens returns at best on a concentrated book.

Same-day capital turns could give decent annualized return, but absolute profit is tiny, title companies may refuse double closes, and the customer base (wholesalers) carries consumer-protection and mortgage-fraud red flags. Stuck-capital tail risk. No evidence on fees or volume.

Not a from-scratch entry: record says it is viable only after 3+ years of documented loan performance. Raising LP capital without track record is near-impossible; securities compliance and fixed costs need $10M+ AUM. Potentially valuable holdco engine later, irrelevant in yr3-5 base case.
red_flags: Requires multi-year track record the founder lacks

rationale: Clean, low-capital, delegable field-service model with recurring per-draw demand and no license for inspections; AI photo/report tooling helps. But per-inspection pricing is guessed, unit value small (~$75-150 contribution), national vendor networks compete, construction-cycle exposed. Needs volume density to reach $100k.

Best structural quality in packet: regulator-expected recurring demand, identifiable buyers (FDIC data), fragmented competition, delegable analyst roles, durable AI spreading/memo advantage. But pricing and outsourcing share MISSING, founder cannot be the reviewer, credibility wall and long cycles; bank consolidation shrinks base. $500k ceiling unproven.
red_flags: Depends on recruiting a credible ex-CCO
Examiner acceptance of AI-assisted review MISSING

rationale: 36% all-in APR cap against subprime losses at tiny scale makes returns likely negative; licensing requirements MISSING; capital-bound with data disadvantage versus incumbents. Record itself says no viable entry at $100k.

Recurring exams (1-4x/yr per borrower), often borrower-reimbursed, and demand rises in credit stress. But tiny specialized buyer group, relationship-driven vendor approval, scarce experienced examiners needed from day one, founder has no collateral-audit expertise, pricing MISSING.

Sticky recurring fees deducted from collections and highly SOP-able, but needs 500-2,000 loans to matter and 24 months to profit; national private-note servicers already price low; per-loan fees MISSING; licensing scope (consumer loans, Collection Agency Act) unresolved.

Real capital scarcity for licensees, but tiny Illinois buyer set, few specialty lenders, no economics data, and federal-illegality banking/AML risk on fee receipts. Relationship-driven, solo, Illinois-bound.

Graduation step, not an entry: aggregator approval and warehouse lines need track record and net worth likely above $100k; repurchase and hedge risk. Correspondent premiums MISSING. Could add margin to WS01-011 after 2-3 years of clean volume.
